## 🔒 Claimed — `domain:cli` seat (#6024), R39

Session `session_01UjujZN219uFzBhSYfMykCd`, identity `os-litant`. Branch **`claude/issue-12573-rest-test-typecheck-paydown`**.

⛔ Clause ② does not apply — test-layer type repairs behind an existing gate.

**Serial**: [PR #12570](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/12570) merged as `3f41a2152`, so the program and the ledger are on `main`. ⚠️ [PR #12421](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/12421) is **still open** and its diff (re-derived from the PR itself, ⛔ not inherited) is five files, one of which is `packages/rest/src/rest.test.ts`.

---

## The ledger as landed, and the fence read against it

```
src/export-integration.test.ts                     17   ← 46% of the whole debt
src/import-integration.test.ts                      3
src/rest-meta-save-receipt-envelope.test.ts         3
src/import-job-integration.test.ts                  2
… 8 files at 1 each                                 8
src/rest.test.ts                                    4   ⛔ FENCED by PR #12421
```

⇒ **12 files, 33 errors are yours. ⛔ `src/rest.test.ts` and its entry of 4 are not.** ⭐ The concentration is entirely outside the fence, so this card loses nothing to it.

---

## Rulings

### 1 · ⭐ TEST THE LEDGER'S OWN HYPOTHESIS BEFORE REPAIRING ANYTHING

The ledger's `_comment` states a cause:

> *"almost all of them fixture literals annotated with a schema **OUTPUT** type (`z.infer`) while holding an authored **INPUT** literal."*

⛔ **Do not take that on faith and ⛔ do not start repairing file by file.** Read the errors first and answer, with numbers: **how many of the 33 are that one shape?** If the answer is "most", this is **one annotation decision applied N times**, not 33 repairs — and the right diff is small and uniform. If the answer is "few", the comment is wrong and ⭐ **that is itself the finding**, worth more than the paydown.

⚠️ #12542 already showed this exact ledger's *previous* number (155) was largely a measurement of a misconfigured check, not of the tests. ⛔ Do not assume the residue is all genuine.

### 2 · Start where the mass is, and expect ONE story

`src/export-integration.test.ts` carries **17 of 37**, and #12542 measured 13 of those as a single `TS18048` class (possibly-undefined). ⚠️ That class did **not exist** in the old 155 at all — it became visible only once the imports above it resolved to real types. ⇒ ⛔ do not pattern-match it to the `z.infer` story without checking; it may be a different, and more real, defect.

Separately, **14 `TS2554`** — *"Expected 2-5 arguments, but got 1"* — span **five** files with the same message. ⭐ That reads as one call-signature story. Confirm or refute it explicitly.

### 3 · ⛔ The forbidden moves, and one of them is subtle

- ⛔ **Never raise a number** in `test-typecheck-debt.json`. *"Raising a debt ledger's ceiling to absorb your own new errors is the gate-weakening floor."*
- ⛔ No `@ts-expect-error`, no `any`, no `as unknown as`, no `exclude` entry, no strictness change in `tsconfig.test.json`.
- ⚠️ **The subtle one**: there are **zero `TS2578`** in this layer today, which means both existing `@ts-expect-error` directives (`src/rest.test.ts`, `src/rest-api-plugin-slot-lookups.test.ts`) are **live**, not phantom. ⛔ Adding a directive that is not itself a live pin would put an unused-directive error into a layer that currently has none — and it would look like a repair.

### 4 · The ratchet is EXACT in three directions — every one of them reds

From the ledger's own comment: **a file that gains errors is red; a file that loses them is red until its number is re-recorded; a file that reaches zero is red until its entry is deleted.**

⇒ every repair must re-record or delete its entry **in the same commit**. ⭐ Regenerate with `pnpm --filter @objectstack/rest gen:test-typecheck-debt` rather than hand-editing — a hand-edited ledger is a number nobody measured. ⛔ But then **read the regenerated diff** and confirm it moved only where you worked; a regenerator that silently rewrites an untouched entry is telling you something.

### 5 · Anti-vacuity — prove the gate still says no

⛔ A green after a paydown is indistinguishable from a green after the program stopped compiling anything. Before trusting it:

- `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --noEmit --listFiles` and assert the **149** test files are still in the program. State the number.
- Plant one real type error in a file you repaired, show the gate exits non-zero and **names that file**, restore, and prove the restore **by blob hash and an empty `git diff HEAD`** — ⛔ never by an exit code. `git checkout HEAD -- <absolute path>`, never bare; trap on `EXIT INT TERM`; mutation confirmed on disk (anchored grep count + blob hash) before any verdict is read.

### 6 · ⛔ A repair must not change what a test asserts

⭐ This is the line that matters most here. These are type errors in **fixtures** — the risk is "fixing" a type by changing the value, and thereby changing what the test measures while it stays green. ⛔ If a repair requires altering a fixture's *data* rather than its *annotation*, stop and report that file: it is a test-semantics question, not a typing one.

### 7 · Standing

- ⛔ **Never** touch `content/docs/releases/**`. ⛔ Do not edit `packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts` or anything in `packages/client`.
- ⭐ **Report what you measure; ⛔ do not reconcile.** Distrust every number above. This round a dispatch order's census was off by +2, a card's by −2, one card's body was wrong twice, two of five line anchors were wrong, and a ruling of mine contradicted itself and had to be settled by measuring 209 against 22.
- ⚠️ **GitHub writes work via the MCP GitHub tools.** Raw REST with `$GITHUB_TOKEN` is 403 (14-char env token). ⚠️ The **additive** label endpoint is also 403 — fallback is **read, union, whole-set write, then read back**. File out-of-scope findings yourself, **unlabelled**.
- Heavy runs via `OS_VERIFY_LOCK_SLOT=issue-12573 bash scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh -c "…"`, detached and polled. ⛔ exit 99 and exit 143 both mean nothing ran; the `VERDICT` line is the authority.
- Gate families from `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`; exit codes **before any pipe**. ⚠️ 9 `packages/spec` families under "THE LAYOUT MOVED" are **#12514** — ⛔ do not refile.
- ⚠️ Expect ~20–30 minutes in the merge queue after arming; **one red push costs a whole extra queue round**, which is more expensive than any amount of verification. Get it right once.

## 🔓 Stand-down — claim released. ⛔ Nothing pushed, ⭐ but ruling 1's measurement was DONE

`domain:cli` seat (#6024), session `session_01UjujZN219uFzBhSYfMykCd`. Reverted to `pm:queue`, unassigned.

**Cause**: this session's dev-agent pool hit a hard account limit — *"You've hit your weekly limit · resets 6pm (UTC)"* — and **five** dev agents were terminated mid-round at ~12:20Z. ⛔ Nothing about this card is implicated.

### State

```
branch  claude/issue-12573-rest-test-typecheck-paydown
head    3f41a2152   ← unchanged from the base it was cut at; NOTHING pushed
```

⚠️ The worktree died with the agent, so **no code survived**.

### ⭐ What DID survive, and it is the expensive half

The dev's last transmission before termination:

> **"All four stories confirmed with exact counts. Now the two TS2345 sites."**

⇒ **Ruling 1 — the one thing the order said to do before touching any code — was completed.** The ledger's `_comment` hypothesis (*"fixture literals annotated with a schema OUTPUT type (`z.infer`) while holding an authored INPUT literal"*) was tested against the 33 errors and resolved into **four confirmed stories with exact counts**, and the dev had worked down to the last two `TS2345` sites.

⚠️ **Those counts are lost.** ⛔ Do not treat "four stories" as a finding — it is a fragment, not a measurement anyone can check. ⭐ But it is strong evidence the paydown is **structured, not a long tail**, which is what ruling 1 was written to find out, and it means the next dev should expect to reach the same shape quickly rather than budget for 33 independent repairs.

### For whoever resumes

Start again at ruling 1 — ⛔ it is cheap to redo and ⛔ nobody may inherit a number they cannot check. Expect roughly: `export-integration.test.ts` ×17 (13 of them one `TS18048` class), `TS2554` ×14 across five files as one call-signature story, `TS2345` ×5, `TS7006` ×4, `TS6133` ×1.

⚠️ **Re-derive the fence.** [PR #12421](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/12421) held `packages/rest/src/rest.test.ts` (4 of the 37) at dispatch time — check whether it still does, from that PR's **own diff**. `origin/main` is now past `5a22dd762`.

The rulings in the claim comment (`5424867477`) all still stand — in particular ruling 6: ⛔ **a repair must not change what a test asserts**; if it needs a fixture's *data* rather than its *annotation*, stop and report.

## ✅ ACCEPT — PR #12625. ⭐ And #12624 is the best finding of this round

`domain:cli` seat (#6024), session `session_01UjujZN219uFzBhSYfMykCd`. Verified against `origin/main`, not the report.

### ⭐ Ruling 1 fired, and the refutation is airtight

The ledger's `_comment` claims *"almost all of them fixture literals annotated with a schema OUTPUT type (`z.infer`) while holding an authored INPUT literal."* Measured: **0 of 33.** I re-ran it — `z.infer` returns **zero** across the ledgered files, and the positive control (`expect` → **65** hits in `export-integration.test.ts` alone) proves the search instrument works. ⭐ A zero with a working control is a measurement; a zero alone is a guess.

### ⭐⭐ And you did not stop at "the comment is wrong" — you found why, and then found what keeps it wrong

**Why**: that clause is #5478/#5543's finding, and **#5543 was closed as completed on 2026-08-08 by [PR #6786](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/6786)**. This ledger was created **18 days later** and stamped with the already-fixed cause.

**What keeps it wrong** — `scripts/check-test-typecheck.mts`:

```
:107  const LEDGER_COMMENT =
:111    'almost all of them fixture literals annotated with a schema OUTPUT type (`z.infer`) while holding …'
:247  if (!fs.existsSync(LEDGER_PATH)) return { _comment: LEDGER_COMMENT, entries: {} };
:258  const ledger: Ledger = { _comment: LEDGER_COMMENT, entries };
```

⇒ **every regeneration re-stamps it, and `--update` overwrites any correction.** ⭐ You corrected the prose, re-ran the regenerator, and **watched the refuted claim come back**. That is not a stale comment — it is a **self-restoring falsehood**, immune to the ordinary repair.

⚠️ **And it is worse than #12624 states.** I read `packages/client/test-typecheck-debt.json`: it asserts that cause over `"entries": {}` — and its own trailing prose explains that ADR-0122 phase 2 (#6083) **emptied** that ledger *because* "all three remaining files were exactly the conflation described above… the flip made the bare name mean the INPUT type, so they compile with no edit."

⇒ ⭐ **The cause was true for `packages/client`, was FIXED there, and the generator has been mechanically reproducing the solved problem's explanation onto every package since — including packages where it was never true.** A fossil, re-cast on every run. That is the durable form of the defect class this lane has filed five cards on this round (#12498 · #12561 · #12563 · #12618 · #12620): not a false explanation that *rotted*, but one that **regenerates**.

### Verified on the work itself

- **17 of 33 paid**, both classes annotation-only (`TS18048` ×13 via non-null assertion at the two `getRoutes().find()` lookups — the form **six green siblings** in this package already use; `TS7006` ×4 via `unknown[]`). ⭐ **Both erase at compile time; neither emits different JavaScript.** That is the cleanest possible answer to ruling 6.
- **Ledger regenerated, not hand-edited**; 4 entries deleted, `export-integration` re-recorded **17 → 4**, every untouched entry byte-identical — ⭐ **including the fenced `rest.test.ts: 4`.** ⇒ ruling 4 held and the fence held.
- **37 → 20 errors, 13 → 9 files, no number raised.** Ruling 3 held.
- ⭐ **The planted-error leg chose the right file**: one this PR repaired *and whose entry it deletes*, so the file is now **unlisted** and any error must red. Gate exited 1 and **named it**. Restore proven by blob hash (`a46e4c50` → `078d4759` → `a46e4c50`), `git diff HEAD` empty. ⛔ Not by an exit code.
- **`--re-measure`'s first refusal reported as a PREREQUISITE REFUSAL, not a red** — then re-run on the full closure exactly as `lint.yml` does: *"31 ledger entr(ies) re-measured … none above its recorded number."* ✔
- **`skip-changeset` reasoned from the rule, not recalled**: `packages/rest` publishes `files: ['dist', …]`, this PR touches only excluded test sources plus the ledger ⇒ nothing published moves; and `check-empty-changeset.mjs` documents that an empty-frontmatter changeset is a **real input** to the changesets action and buys nothing the label does not. ⭐ Measuring which of two near-identical options is correct, rather than picking the familiar one.

## ⚖️ The three open questions

### Q1 — **A. Keep `Part of #12573`.** My order was wrong to say `Fixes`

I wrote `Fixes #12573`. With 17 of 33 paid and the remaining 16 blocked on #12623's contract decision, closing the card would **orphan the remainder** — no card would hold the 20 errors still ledgered. ⭐ And you flagged the conflict instead of silently satisfying the order, which is exactly what the standing clause asks for. ⛔ C costs a card for nothing.

### Q2 — ⛔ **Not mine to rule. Correctly escalated to #12623.**

A public-API widening on `SchemaRegistry.registerObject` is a maintainer's call and I will not take it from a test-layer paydown. ⭐ But the escalation is well-armed, and worth restating so the decision is cheap: **the producer is the half out of step** — its own sibling `registerItem` already declares `packageId` optional, both feed the identical `applyProtection(item, { packageId })`, and that helper's docstring says the package-less call *deliberately* leaves fixtures without `_provenance`. ⇒ option B would stamp `_provenance` onto **82** fixtures, which is a test-semantics change at 82 sites masquerading as a compile fix.

⚠️ And the reach is the part that makes it urgent rather than tidy: **68 more identical call sites in `objectql` (55), `runtime` (9) and `plugins` (4) — none of which has a test-layer tsc program**, so the same latent error is **unmeasured** there. ⭐ `packages/rest` is not where this defect lives; it is merely the first package with an instrument that can see it.

### Q3 — **B now, C as the durable fix.** Agreed, and B *is* ruling 6

`headers` / `path` are the fixture's **data**, not its annotation — so you stopped and reported, which is what ruling 6 says to do. ⛔ `as any` was correctly refused even though the surrounding files use it. ⭐ C (a typed `IHttpRequest` builder) is right precisely because it makes the required fields explicit **once** instead of letting each migrating site invent its own header and path values — which is how a fixture's data drifts silently.

### One small correction to my own stand-down, noted and accepted

You report the branch ref already existed at `3f41a2152` when you pushed, whereas my stand-down said nothing was pushed. ⭐ Both true: the **ref** existed at the old base, no **work commit** did. That is the same three-legged lesson from #12543 — *local worktree, remote branch, PR* — with a fourth wrinkle: **a branch ref existing is not work existing.**

**Un-drafted. Enqueueing on every check green — ⚠️ latest-per-name.**
